score.note: Re-measured 2026-08-27, unchanged from the prior baseline: structurally identical to the reference at old-agbcc -O1 (all thirteen instructions match one-for-one in mnemonic, operand shape, and branch structure); the only residual is one uniform register rotation -- the candidate's serial scratch register is r0 where the reference uses r2 (and consequently r2/r3 where the reference uses r3). Root-caused this session by invoking alchemy-gcc/dist/agbcc/old_agbcc directly on the preprocessed source with -dlgr and reading the .lreg/.greg dumps (see rejected_experiments below for the full derivation): this build's local-alloc find_free_reg does NOT honor arm.h's REG_ALLOC_ORDER {r3,r2,r1,r0,...} bias for this owner's qtys -- it hands out the first ascending free register instead (r0, else r1, else r2, ...). track (r1) is always excluded since it lives the whole function; the dead first parameter (r0) is genuinely dead by the time the flow graph reaches the scratch pseudo's block, so r0 is free and wins every time in this build, then the reload-forced load of the pre-OR flags byte takes the next free ascending register (r2). For the reference's r2/r3 pair to appear, r0 would have to still read as live at that point -- and no legitimate source construct achieves that: a probe with `asm volatile("" :: "r"(unused))` right at entry (tested this session, not adopted -- forcing register liveness through inline asm is exactly the kind of register-assignment forcing CONTRIBUTING.md prohibits, and this was a diagnostic probe only) still let r0 free by the time the first store's scratch register is chosen, since GCC's liveness naturally recomputes the dead range after the trivial touch. Genuinely keeping r0 live (a real use, or a non-void return) requires emitting real code that breaks the verified 13-instruction match (already established by the return-value and -ffixed-r0 experiments below). This is the class-2 known-dead-end register-letter residual from this session's catalog, now with a first-principles compiler-internals confirmation rather than only cross-owner pattern-matching.
